business_problem: DGW Group needed to jump-start digital transformation by modernizing its data center, improving reliability for Indonesian operations, and strengthening security around workloads and enterprise communications.
solution_summary: DGW Group used Alibaba Cloud as the basis for a data-center modernization program that combined migration, security, and managed communications. The company outsourced core data-center operations to Alibaba Cloud in Indonesia, gaining access to a provider with local regions and multiple availability zones that could support compliance and availability requirements. Around the migrated workloads, DGW Group implemented a multi-layer security design: Anti-DDoS services protect at the network layer by identifying and scrubbing malicious traffic, while Web Application Firewall handles application-layer filtering for exposed services. The company also adopted Alimail as a managed enterprise email platform built on Alibaba's large-scale security architecture, allowing DGW Group to move messaging off local systems while maintaining availability and protection. Together these services give the agricultural group a more resilient cloud operating model, better uptime targets, and a cleaner base for broader digital transformation work in Indonesia.
business_outcome: DGW Group improved uptime, increased the resilience of its application estate, and offloaded key infrastructure and email operations to Alibaba Cloud.
architecture_clues: Uses cloud regions and multiple availability zones in Indonesia
Applies multi-layer security across network and application layers
Alimail replaces local email operations with a managed service
The migration is positioned as a jump-start for digital transformation

data_flow: Application traffic reaches DGW Group workloads running on Alibaba Cloud, Anti-DDoS screens hostile network traffic, WAF filters web requests at the application layer, and Alimail handles business email on a separate managed communications plane.
